label: Heart
acute_loss: Pump or conduction failure can be immediately fatal.
persistent_loss: Lost contractile reserve and scar can persist.
repair: Adult cardiomyocyte renewal is limited, not absent.
management: Mechanical support/transplant are not routine compensation for target-mediated injury.
rationale: Protect bulk heart because expression cannot exclude contractile or conduction cells.
evidence_scope: Human antigen-directed T-cell injury or depletion provides a clinical anchor; findings remain receptor/product-specific and may not resolve every subset in this rule.

label: Blood vessels and endothelium
acute_loss: Leak, thrombosis and disrupted perfusion can injure several organs.
persistent_loss: Vascular remodeling and ischemic injury can persist.
repair: Endothelial repair depends on injury extent and the vascular bed.
management: No general replacement for distributed vascular function.
rationale: A broad vascular label does not locate a safely expendable vessel population.
evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

label: Brain and spinal cord
acute_loss: Circuit disruption can cause major neurological disability or death.
persistent_loss: Neuronal loss and disconnection may be irreversible.
repair: Repair varies by lineage; preservation of some progenitors does not restore complex circuits.
management: Rehabilitation is not replacement of lost circuits.
rationale: Small specialized populations can have high consequence; bulk dilution cannot establish safety.
evidence_scope: Human antigen-directed T-cell injury or depletion provides a clinical anchor; findings remain receptor/product-specific and may not resolve every subset in this rule.

label: Peripheral nerve
acute_loss: Motor, sensory and autonomic failure may be disabling or life-threatening.
persistent_loss: Denervation and failed reinnervation can persist.
repair: Axonal repair requires surviving neurons, Schwann cells and permissive paths.
management: Support does not guarantee functional restoration.
rationale: Potential regeneration is insufficient for a default downgrade of a mixed nerve sample.
evidence_scope: Physiological/clinical analogy; no direct selective immune-depletion study is cited for this call.

label: Eye and retina
acute_loss: Injury can cause vision loss.
persistent_loss: Retinal or optic damage may be irreversible.
repair: Corneal epithelial repair and retinal neural replacement are different processes.
management: Local treatment or grafting applies only to selected compartments.
rationale: A bulk eye sample cannot establish restriction to replaceable surface epithelium.
evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

label: Inner ear
acute_loss: Hearing and balance may be lost.
persistent_loss: Sensory deficits can persist despite suppression of inflammation.
repair: Limited vestibular replacement in mice does not establish human cochlear regeneration.
management: Assistive devices do not fully replace native sensory function.
rationale: Critical sensory disability is included in Vital even when injury is not lethal.
evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

label: Lung and bronchus
acute_loss: Diffuse injury can cause edema and respiratory failure.
persistent_loss: Fibrosis and impaired clearance can persist.
repair: AT2 and airway progenitors can repair finite injury but may be targeted themselves.
management: Ventilation treats failure without proving recovery or stopping recognition.
rationale: Bulk lung includes alveolar, vascular and regenerative compartments; use explicit cell subsets for narrower calls.
evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

label: Liver
acute_loss: Loss of detoxification and synthetic function can be life-threatening.
persistent_loss: Fibrosis, cholestasis and depleted regenerative reserve can persist.
repair: Hepatocytes regenerate; biliary compensation depends on surviving lineages.
management: Transplantation is not a general workaround for persistent antigen recognition.
rationale: High regenerative capacity does not make widespread or repeated hepatic injury manageable.
evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

label: Kidney
acute_loss: Filtration, electrolyte and volume failure can be life-threatening.
persistent_loss: Podocyte depletion and repeated tubular injury can cause sclerosis and fibrosis.
repair: Tubules and podocytes have different repair capacity; both matter in bulk kidney.
management: Dialysis is substantial support and does not prevent all injury consequences.
rationale: Retain high protection for both irreversible glomerular loss and sustained tubular injury.
evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

label: Pancreas
acute_loss: Inflammatory injury and endocrine failure can cause acute severe illness.
persistent_loss: Diabetes and digestive insufficiency can require lifelong support.
repair: Endocrine and exocrine populations differ; bulk does not establish isolated beta-cell exposure.
management: Insulin and enzymes replace selected outputs, not all acute organ injury.
rationale: A broad pancreas signal retains Vital; isolated cell populations are assessed separately.
evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

label: Adrenal gland
acute_loss: Glucocorticoid/mineralocorticoid failure can precipitate crisis.
persistent_loss: Deficits require continuing replacement and stress dosing.
repair: Reliable restoration after destructive immune injury is unestablished.
management: Replacement mitigates deficiency but requires sustained clinical management.
rationale: Bulk adrenal cannot exclude multiple axes or rapidly destabilizing cortical injury.
evidence_scope: Physiological/clinical analogy; no direct selective immune-depletion study is cited for this call.

label: Pituitary gland
acute_loss: ACTH failure and disturbed water balance may be life-threatening.
persistent_loss: Several hormone deficits may persist.
repair: Clinical inflammatory injury shows incomplete hormonal recovery.
management: Multiple hormones and fluid balance may need ongoing support.
rationale: A mixed pituitary sample cannot establish exposure limited to a readily compensated axis.
evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

label: Thyroid gland
acute_loss: Destructive thyroiditis can release hormone and cause symptomatic thyrotoxicosis.
persistent_loss: Hypothyroidism may be permanent.
repair: Functional recovery is variable; the rationale is replaceable output rather than guaranteed regeneration.
management: Thyroid hormone replacement is an established form of compensation.
rationale: Manageable is conditional on controlling acute injury and maintaining replacement; not Disposable.
evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

label: Parathyroid gland
acute_loss: Calcium disturbance can affect neuromuscular and cardiac function.
persistent_loss: Persistent hormone deficiency can require complex supplementation.
repair: Reliable regeneration after extensive immune injury is unestablished.
management: Replacement of mineral balance is feasible but imperfect.
rationale: Persistent homeostatic consequences justify more protection than a simple removable-gland analogy.
evidence_scope: Physiological/clinical analogy; no direct selective immune-depletion study is cited for this call.

label: Salivary glands
acute_loss: Inflammation can impair oral intake and secretion.
persistent_loss: Severe dryness, dental injury and infection risk can persist.
repair: Clinical symptomatic recovery need not restore salivary flow.
management: Symptomatic management incompletely replaces gland function.
rationale: Local accessibility does not ensure recovery of secretory tissue.
evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

label: Bone marrow
acute_loss: Loss of blood-cell production can cause infection, anemia and bleeding.
persistent_loss: Stem-cell or niche depletion can prevent recovery.
repair: Requires surviving progenitors and a functional stromal niche.
management: Transfusion and transplantation do not establish general target tolerability.
rationale: Marrow is a mixed regenerative organ; mature B-cell experience cannot be generalized to it.
evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

label: Blood
acute_loss: Distributed cell depletion can compromise oxygen delivery, hemostasis or host defence.
persistent_loss: Persistent targeting can prevent hematopoietic replenishment.
repair: Renewal depends on spared marrow and antigen distribution during maturation.
management: Lineage-specific support exists but is not equivalent across cell types.
rationale: Bulk blood must not inherit a mature B-cell exception.
evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

label: Lymph nodes
acute_loss: Inflammation can disrupt immune organization and drainage.
persistent_loss: Lymphatic and stromal injury may cause lasting dysfunction.
repair: Removal of one node does not model depletion of all nodes or shared lineages.
management: No complete replacement for distributed nodal organization.
rationale: Distinguish circulating immune cells from resident lymphatic and stromal structure.
evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

label: Spleen
acute_loss: Inflammatory or vascular injury can be severe.
persistent_loss: Functional asplenia increases long-term infection risk.
repair: Other immune organs compensate incompletely.
management: Vaccination and infection management reduce, but do not remove, consequences.
rationale: Surgical survival supports partial compensation, not a low-consequence or Disposable designation.
evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

label: Thymus
acute_loss: Immediate effects vary with age and pre-existing immune reserve.
persistent_loss: Loss of T-cell renewal may have delayed consequences.
repair: Adult involution does not establish absence of continuing function.
management: No routine full replacement of thymic function.
rationale: Adult thymectomy associations argue for protection; pediatric risk requires separate review.
evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

label: Tonsil
acute_loss: In-situ inflammation, swelling or bleeding can still be serious.
persistent_loss: Local organ loss is often compensated by other immune sites.
repair: Allowance rests on local removal tolerance, not regeneration.
management: Surgery is a local precedent, not evidence for systemic immune-lineage depletion.
rationale: The exception requires restriction to tonsillar tissue and excludes the same lymphocyte lineage elsewhere.
evidence_scope: Physiological/clinical analogy; no direct selective immune-depletion study is cited for this call.

label: Small intestine
acute_loss: Diffuse barrier failure can cause sepsis and fluid loss.
persistent_loss: Extensive loss can compromise nutrient absorption and renewal.
repair: Crypt alternatives can compensate for selected insults; shared progenitor targeting changes the result.
management: Nutritional support does not guarantee control of destructive enteritis.
rationale: Renewal alone does not justify lowering a whole-organ small-intestine finding.
evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

label: Colon and rectum
acute_loss: Colitis can cause severe diarrhea, bleeding or perforation.
persistent_loss: Persistent targeting can cause chronic injury and impaired repair.
repair: Mature cells renew if regenerative compartments survive.
management: Clinical recovery after some TCR injuries is not universal rescue.
rationale: Bulk bowel does not establish restriction to mature replaceable epithelium.
evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

label: Esophagus and stomach
acute_loss: Mucosal injury can impair intake, bleed or perforate.
persistent_loss: Stricture and gland loss may be persistent.
repair: Renewal requires surviving progenitors and control of inflammation.
management: Supportive therapy and local access do not guarantee recovery.
rationale: Mixed mucosa, glands and muscle merit protection even where some lining cells renew.
evidence_scope: Physiological/clinical analogy; no direct selective immune-depletion study is cited for this call.

label: Oral and upper-airway mucosa
acute_loss: Injury can impair swallowing, intake or airway patency.
persistent_loss: Scarring, dryness and sensory deficits can persist.
repair: Surface renewal differs from gland, neural and muscle repair.
management: Local treatment is conditional on injury extent and persistence.
rationale: Bulk mucosal labels cannot exclude important underlying structures.
evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

label: Appendix
acute_loss: In-situ inflammation may perforate or spread.
persistent_loss: Organ absence can be tolerated after controlled removal.
repair: Removal tolerance, not regeneration, underlies the exception.
management: Surgery is not equivalent to uncontrolled antigen-directed destruction.
rationale: Restriction must be to appendix, not a shared bowel or immune lineage.
evidence_scope: Physiological/clinical analogy; no direct selective immune-depletion study is cited for this call.

label: Gallbladder
acute_loss: Inflammation, obstruction or bile leakage can be serious.
persistent_loss: Loss of storage function is generally compensated after removal.
repair: Allowance rests on organ-removal experience.
management: Adjacent bile ducts and liver are not covered by the exception.
rationale: Local removability supports a narrow allowance rather than permission for generic biliary cells.
evidence_scope: Physiological/clinical analogy; no direct selective immune-depletion study is cited for this call.

label: Bladder and ureter
acute_loss: Inflammation and obstruction can compromise urinary drainage.
persistent_loss: Stricture, poor compliance and barrier dysfunction can persist.
repair: Urothelial regeneration depends on intact progenitor/stromal signaling.
management: Diversion or reconstruction is substantial intervention, not ordinary compensation.
rationale: Renewing urothelium does not make distributed or muscular injury low consequence.
evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

label: Skin
acute_loss: Extensive epithelial loss threatens barrier, fluid balance and infection control.
persistent_loss: Scarring, chronic wounds and lost appendages can persist.
repair: Repair depends on viable epidermal and appendage progenitors and injury extent.
management: Local treatment applies to selected injuries; extensive loss needs systemic care.
rationale: Bulk skin is broader than cutaneous melanocytes or hair follicles and must retain barrier concern.
evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

label: Cutaneous melanocytes
acute_loss: Inflammation may accompany pigment-cell killing.
persistent_loss: Depigmentation may persist.
repair: Return of pigment is not required for the conditional allowance.
management: Sun protection and skin surveillance may be required.
rationale: Cutaneous restriction is essential; eye and inner-ear pigment cells are excluded.
evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

label: Hair follicles
acute_loss: Follicular inflammation can be painful and extensive.
persistent_loss: Alopecia can be permanent after stem-cell injury.
repair: Regrowth depends on the surviving follicular stem-cell niche.
management: Loss is generally compatible with systemic function, but can be consequential to the patient.
rationale: An explicit follicular sample can receive a narrow allowance; generic skin stem cells cannot.
evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

label: Adipose tissue
acute_loss: Widespread inflammatory injury may disturb metabolism.
persistent_loss: Generalized fat loss can cause major metabolic dysfunction.
repair: Adult turnover exists but does not imply rapid restoration of widespread loss.
management: Compensation depends strongly on extent, depot and metabolic reserve.
rationale: Conditional lower priority for limited depot injury; pan-adipocyte targeting needs an explicit extent review.
evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

label: Skeletal muscle
acute_loss: Respiratory weakness or extensive myonecrosis may be life-threatening.
persistent_loss: Weakness and fibrosis may persist if regenerative support is damaged.
repair: Satellite cells and supportive fibroblasts are required for effective repair.
management: Support and rehabilitation do not replace destroyed respiratory muscle.
rationale: A generic muscle label cannot exclude diaphragm or distributed injury.
evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

label: Smooth muscle
acute_loss: Vascular or visceral contractile failure can threaten perfusion and organ function.
persistent_loss: Dysmotility or structural remodeling can persist.
repair: Repair is site dependent and not established from a generic label.
management: No single replacement applies to all smooth-muscle sites.
rationale: Unknown anatomical site retains high protection; local uterine membership remains a separate scope.
evidence_scope: Physiological/clinical analogy; no direct selective immune-depletion study is cited for this call.

label: Cartilage
acute_loss: Location determines consequences, including airway support.
persistent_loss: Matrix damage and deformity may be persistent.
repair: Adult articular collagen turns over slowly; this is indirect evidence for cell-loss effects.
management: Symptom control does not restore structural integrity.
rationale: Articular evidence supports protection; unknown cartilage site does not justify assuming a harmless joint compartment.
evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

label: Testis
acute_loss: Inflammation can cause pain and endocrine disturbance.
persistent_loss: Fertility and androgen production can be permanently lost.
repair: Germline renewal requires surviving stem and supporting cells.
management: Hormone replacement cannot restore fertility.
rationale: Reproductive expression is a CTA association axis, not evidence that testicular injury is harmless.
evidence_scope: Identity/function evidence only; no direct selective-depletion or immune-injury study is cited for this call.

label: Ovary
acute_loss: Inflammation may disrupt ovarian function.
persistent_loss: Oocyte depletion can cause irreversible infertility and endocrine failure.
repair: Finite reserve differs from a renewable epithelial barrier.
management: Hormone replacement does not replace oocyte reserve.
rationale: Reproductive membership must not be read as a severity category.
evidence_scope: Identity/function evidence only; no direct selective-depletion or immune-injury study is cited for this call.

label: Reproductive ducts and accessory organs
acute_loss: Injury can cause inflammation, obstruction and mucosal damage.
persistent_loss: Infertility, scarring and functional losses may be persistent.
repair: Repair differs between glands, ducts, muscle and mucosa.
management: Selected removal is possible but not a general model for distributed immune injury.
rationale: Keep hazard separate from the project reproductive permission; broad organs contain several important cell populations.
evidence_scope: Identity/function evidence only; no direct selective-depletion or immune-injury study is cited for this call.

label: Mammary tissue
acute_loss: Inflammation may be substantial, particularly during lactation.
persistent_loss: Loss can impair lactation and cause permanent structural changes.
repair: Epithelial plasticity depends on physiological state and surviving progenitors.
management: Systemic survival is compatible with gland loss; patient context remains important.
rationale: Conditional lower priority applies to nonlactating adult context; reproductive membership remains independent.
evidence_scope: Identity/function evidence only; no direct selective-depletion or immune-injury study is cited for this call.

label: Mature airway ciliated cells
acute_loss: Loss impairs clearance; cytotoxic elimination also disrupts epithelial integrity.
persistent_loss: Infection and chronic airway damage can accumulate during sustained depletion.
repair: Spared progenitors permit renewal, but selective depletion did not trigger rapid replacement in mice.
management: Airway clearance and infection treatment do not fully replace ciliary function.
rationale: Lower immediate loss-of-function concern than alveolar failure is plausible; slow renewal and chronic consequences prevent an automatic Manageable allowance.
evidence_scope: Lineage-focused animal depletion/repair evidence supports the mechanism; promoter specificity, injury kinetics and spared alternatives limit translation.

label: Airway club cells
acute_loss: Secretory and airway progenitor function may be lost.
persistent_loss: Repeated depletion can exhaust repair and leave lasting peribronchiolar fibrosis.
repair: Club cells themselves provide regenerative capacity; surviving basal or alternative populations may compensate only conditionally.
management: Ventilation treats failure without proving recovery or stopping recognition.
rationale: Club cells cannot be treated as merely replaceable mature luminal cells; persistent loss directly threatens airway repair.
evidence_scope: Lineage-focused animal depletion/repair evidence supports the mechanism; promoter specificity, injury kinetics and spared alternatives limit translation.

label: Airway basal cells
acute_loss: Depletion removes a principal conducting-airway regenerative compartment; immediate effects depend on existing epithelial integrity.
persistent_loss: Persistent loss can impair re-epithelialization and contribute to airway fibrosis.
repair: Surviving secretory cells can dedifferentiate after finite basal-cell loss in mice; shared targeting can remove this alternative.
management: Respiratory support does not replace the regenerative pool or establish control of continuing recognition.
rationale: Protect principal airway progenitors while recording secretory-cell dedifferentiation as conditional counterevidence.
evidence_scope: Lineage-focused animal depletion/repair evidence supports the mechanism; promoter specificity, injury kinetics and spared alternatives limit translation.

label: Mature airway goblet cells
acute_loss: Isolated loss principally disrupts mucus defence rather than alveolar gas exchange.
persistent_loss: Loss of secretory defence may permit recurrent infection and chronic injury.
repair: Secretory-state plasticity is possible, but replacement cells may remain targets.
management: Airway clearance and infection treatment do not reproduce all mucus-defense functions.
rationale: Mucin knockout and altered differentiation are not cytotoxic ablation; sparse direct evidence supports a provisional Protected call.
evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

label: Unresolved airway secretory cells
acute_loss: A broad secretory label may include both mature mucus-producing cells and regenerative club populations.
persistent_loss: Persistent targeting may compromise defense and renewal, depending on the actual cell mixture.
repair: Unknown secretory identity cannot establish spared club or alternative progenitors.
management: Support for mucus clearance does not compensate for loss of regeneration.
rationale: A broad secretory label may include club progenitors or essential gland populations and cannot inherit a mature-goblet downgrade.
evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

label: Airway ionocytes
acute_loss: Selective loss could alter airway ion transport and surface-liquid homeostasis.
persistent_loss: Persistent transport disturbance could impair mucus handling; selective immune-depletion outcomes remain unresolved.
repair: Rarity is not evidence of dispensability, and regeneration after selective immune loss is unestablished.
management: Compensation by other transport-expressing cells is a question for testing, not an established replacement strategy.
rationale: Specialized ion transport supports airway physiology; direct cell-depletion tolerability evidence is insufficient for a lower default.
evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

label: Alveolar type 1 cells
acute_loss: Extensive uncompensated loss can disrupt the gas-exchange epithelial barrier.
persistent_loss: Repeated injury can drive abnormal epithelial repair; barrier dysfunction depends on compensation.
repair: AT2 cells can rapidly flatten and differentiate after finite AT1 injury; persistent recognition may alter repair states.
management: Ventilation treats failure without proving recovery or stopping recognition.
rationale: Barrier function merits high protection; record rapid AT2 compensation rather than describing AT1 cells as irreplaceable.
evidence_scope: Lineage-focused animal depletion/repair evidence supports the mechanism; promoter specificity, injury kinetics and spared alternatives limit translation.

label: Alveolar type 2 cells
acute_loss: Loss threatens surfactant function and can initiate edema and respiratory failure.
persistent_loss: Depletion can impair alveolar repair and initiate fibrosis.
repair: Recovery depends on surviving AT2/alternative progenitors, injury kinetics and supporting tissue.
management: Ventilation supports gas exchange but does not restore the surfactant-producing regenerative compartment.
rationale: Surfactant output and alveolar renewal combine immediate and regenerative consequences; animal depletion and antigen-specific injury support major hazard.
evidence_scope: Lineage-focused animal depletion/repair evidence supports the mechanism; promoter specificity, injury kinetics and spared alternatives limit translation.

label: Unresolved alveolar epithelium
acute_loss: Diffuse injury can cause edema and respiratory failure.
persistent_loss: Persistent injury can compromise alveolar repair and produce fibrosis.
repair: A broad pneumocyte label does not establish whether AT2 repair is spared.
management: Ventilation treats failure without proving recovery or stopping recognition.
rationale: Unresolved pneumocyte labels must not acquire the repair assumptions of an isolated mature subtype.
evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

label: Pulmonary endothelium
acute_loss: Vascular leak, edema and impaired perfusion can disrupt gas exchange.
persistent_loss: Persistent microvascular injury can impair alveolar function and tissue repair.
repair: Alveolar epithelial repair does not establish endothelial recovery; vascular-bed and injury-extent effects matter.
management: Respiratory support does not replace a functioning pulmonary microvascular barrier.
rationale: The alveolar-capillary interface can fail through direct recognition or secondary inflammatory vascular injury.
evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

label: Cardiomyocytes and conduction cells
acute_loss: Pump or conduction failure can be immediately fatal.
persistent_loss: Lost contractile reserve and scar can persist.
repair: Adult cardiomyocyte renewal is limited, not absent.
management: Mechanical support/transplant are not routine compensation for target-mediated injury.
rationale: Limited adult renewal and direct receptor-specific cardiac toxicity support high protection; electrically specialized subsets are not discounted by rarity.
evidence_scope: Human antigen-directed T-cell injury or depletion provides a clinical anchor; findings remain receptor/product-specific and may not resolve every subset in this rule.

label: CNS neurons
acute_loss: Circuit disruption can cause major neurological disability or death.
persistent_loss: Neuronal loss and disconnection may be irreversible.
repair: Repair varies by lineage; preservation of some progenitors does not restore complex circuits.
management: Rehabilitation is not replacement of lost circuits.
rationale: Protect specialized neural circuits even where a small fraction of cells expresses the target.
evidence_scope: Human antigen-directed T-cell injury or depletion provides a clinical anchor; findings remain receptor/product-specific and may not resolve every subset in this rule.

label: Astrocytes and oligodendroglia
acute_loss: Loss of ion buffering, metabolic support or myelin can disrupt neural function.
persistent_loss: Demyelination, secondary axonal injury and disrupted homeostasis can persist.
repair: Repair differs among astrocytes and oligodendrocyte-lineage cells; surviving progenitors do not guarantee restoration under repeated attack.
management: Supportive care cannot replace distributed glial functions.
rationale: Distributed support, myelination and homeostatic roles can make non-neuronal loss disabling; neuron-to-glia equivalence is a mechanistic inference.
evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

label: Ependymal cells
acute_loss: Injury may disturb CSF-facing epithelial and ciliary functions.
persistent_loss: Persistent ventricular-lining injury may alter CSF homeostasis; direct selective clinical evidence is limited.
repair: Airway ciliated-cell replacement is not evidence for adult ependymal repair.
management: Treating downstream CSF disturbances would not necessarily restore the lining.
rationale: CSF-facing homeostasis and ciliary function warrant protection; airway-cilia policy must not be transferred to CNS ependyma.
evidence_scope: Identity/function evidence only; no direct selective-depletion or immune-injury study is cited for this call.

label: Schwann cells
acute_loss: Motor, sensory and autonomic failure may be disabling or life-threatening.
persistent_loss: Denervation and failed reinnervation can persist.
repair: Axonal repair requires surviving neurons, Schwann cells and permissive paths.
management: Support does not guarantee functional restoration.
rationale: Myelination and regeneration support are both at stake; peripheral repair depends on surviving axons and support cells.
evidence_scope: Physiological/clinical analogy; no direct selective immune-depletion study is cited for this call.

label: Retinal neurons and photoreceptors
acute_loss: Injury can cause vision loss.
persistent_loss: Retinal or optic damage may be irreversible.
repair: Adult human retinal circuit replacement is not reliably achieved after destructive loss.
management: Vision aids do not restore native retinal circuits.
rationale: Loss can irreversibly affect visual processing; a whole-eye immune-toxicity precedent does not resolve individual retinal lineages.
evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

label: Retinal pigment epithelium
acute_loss: Loss of retinal pigment epithelial support can compromise photoreceptor function.
persistent_loss: Secondary photoreceptor injury and visual loss may persist.
repair: Restoring an organized functional RPE layer after diffuse immune loss is unestablished.
management: Cutaneous depigmentation experience does not establish compensation for retinal support loss.
rationale: Retinal support differs fundamentally from cutaneous pigment function; retain high protection.
evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

label: Limbal stem/progenitor cells
acute_loss: Injury can cause vision loss.
persistent_loss: Persistent epithelial defects, corneal opacity and loss of vision can follow injury; retinal loss is a separate compartment.
repair: Loss of limbal reserve can prevent sustained corneal resurfacing; transplantation is conditional rescue.
management: Local treatment or grafting applies only to selected compartments.
rationale: Protect the regenerative compartment needed to maintain a transparent corneal surface.
evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

label: Mature corneal epithelial cells
acute_loss: Surface defects can cause pain, infection and impaired vision.
persistent_loss: Persistent epithelial defects and scarring can impair transparency.
repair: Surface renewal depends on spared limbal and basal regenerative populations.
management: Local support and selected grafts do not guarantee recovery during persistent recognition.
rationale: Surface replacement is possible with spared limbal reserve; ulceration and scarring remain important.
evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

label: Corneal endothelium
acute_loss: Loss of endothelial fluid regulation can cause corneal edema and impaired vision.
persistent_loss: Persistent edema and secondary structural changes can impair transparency.

evidence_scope: Identity/function evidence only; no direct selective-depletion or immune-injury study is cited for this call.

label: Inner-ear hair cells
acute_loss: Hearing and balance may be lost.
persistent_loss: Sensory deficits can persist despite suppression of inflammation.
repair: Limited vestibular replacement in mice does not establish human cochlear regeneration.
management: Assistive devices do not fully replace native sensory function.

evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

label: Hepatocytes
acute_loss: Loss of detoxification and synthetic function can be life-threatening.
persistent_loss: Fibrosis, cholestasis and depleted regenerative reserve can persist.
repair: Hepatocytes regenerate; biliary compensation depends on surviving lineages.
management: Transplantation is not a general workaround for persistent antigen recognition.
rationale: Finite-injury regeneration is substantial but depends on survivors; distributed persistent loss threatens metabolic and synthetic function.
evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

label: Cholangiocytes
acute_loss: Bile-duct epithelial injury can impair bile flow and initiate cholestatic inflammation.
persistent_loss: Duct loss, cholestasis and fibrosis can become chronic.
repair: Biliary repair and facultative hepatocyte contribution require surviving responsive populations.

evidence_scope: Compartment-level mechanistic inference; cited clinical or experimental evidence does not quantify receptor-specific human risk.

label: Podocytes
acute_loss: Filtration-barrier disruption can cause substantial proteinuria.
persistent_loss: Progressive glomerulosclerosis and loss of filtration can follow depletion.
repair: Podocyte replacement is limited; remaining cells can compensate only within model-dependent bounds.

rationale: Selective depletion directly supports progressive filtration-barrier failure and sclerosis.
evidence_scope: Lineage-focused animal depletion/repair evidence supports the mechanism; promoter specificity, injury kinetics and spared alternatives limit translation.
